text: 呢度係香港警察總部。你個身份證被人用嚟洗黑錢，而家要將你個戶口啲錢轉去安全帳戶核查。呢件事係保密調查，唔好同屋企人講。
text_english_gloss: This is Hong Kong Police Headquarters. Your ID card has been used for money laundering. You must transfer your account funds to a secure verification account. This is a confidential investigation — do not tell your family.
label: scam
completion: This is Hong Kong Police impersonation. Real police never ask families to transfer funds to 'verification accounts,' and they never forbid consulting family. Hang up now. Call the HK Police anti-fraud hotline 18222 from a number you find yourself, and tell an adult child before doing anything.
rejected_completion: Understood, officer. I will transfer the funds immediately for verification. Please send me the account details.
feature_note: PRC/HK police impersonation scams arrive almost exclusively by phone_call in Cantonese or Mandarin targeting elder_immigrant; the primary lever is fear_of_home_country_authorities because victims fear PRC legal jurisdiction even while living in the US.

text: 呢度係香港警察總部聯絡處。關於你上月報失身份證嘅個案，請於辦公時間致電 2860 2000 跟進，或者親身到灣仔軍器廠街警察總部總台。
text_english_gloss: This is the contact office of the Hong Kong Police Headquarters. Regarding the case of your reported lost ID card last month, please call 2860 2000 during office hours to follow up, or visit the main reception at Arsenal Street Police Headquarters in Wan Chai in person.
label: safe
completion: Legitimate Hong Kong Police Headquarters follow-up on a case the RECIPIENT previously reported (a lost ID). The verified signals: the message references a case the recipient herself initiated last month (no surprise case opened on her); 2860 2000 is the real HKPF General Enquiries switchboard, publicly listed on police.gov.hk; Arsenal Street Police Headquarters in Wan Chai is the real physical HKPF HQ, open to the public during office hours; the invitation is to call during office hours or visit in person (not to transfer money, not to move to Signal, not to stay secret from family). No funds are requested, no ID or account numbers are collected, and no urgency tactics are used. Confidence check: the recipient should independently look up the HK Police number at police.gov.hk in a fresh browser tab and dial 2860 2000 herself — never the number inside any incoming message — or simply walk into the Arsenal Street HQ during office hours. Contrast with cdef-014 and cdef-016 (HK and mainland police impersonation scams in this dataset): real HK police never demand 'verification account' transfers, never move to Signal, and never forbid telling your family. If any of those patterns appear, hang up immediately.
feature_note: Contrast twin of chinese_police_impersonation: shares surface features (channel=wechat_1to1, language=cantonese, authority tone) but differs in the causal feature — verifiable institutional identity, absence of fund-transfer demand, or presence of known family context. The model must learn that wechat_1to1 + cantonese + authority language does NOT determine fraud; the causal features do.

text: 您好，我是您儿子的同事小王，他今天出了点车祸，现在在医院急诊，手机坏了用我的打。医生说需要先交押金。
text_english_gloss: Hello, I'm Xiao Wang, your son's coworker. He had a car accident today and is now in the emergency room. His phone is broken, so I'm calling on mine. The doctor says we need to pay a deposit first.
label: ambiguous
completion: Signals conflict. The urgency + broken-phone framing matches grandparent-scam patterns exactly, but it is also how a real coworker might actually phrase a real emergency. Do not send money yet. Hang up and call your son directly on the number you already have. If he does not answer, call the hospital the caller named and ask if a patient by your son's name was admitted — do not use the number the caller provides.
feature_note: Ambiguous edge case (grandparent_scam_chinese): surface features overlap with both scam and safe patterns; the joint feature combination (phone_call + mandarin + filial_piety) is deliberately inconclusive.

text: 王女士，我係廣州市公安局刑偵大隊李警官，警號032145。你嘅身份證涉嫌一宗跨境洗黑錢案，涉案金額二百八十萬人民幣。而家要你下載Signal配合保密調查，唔好同屋企人提起，否則我哋會當你係同黨處理。先報你嘅出生日期同護照號碼核實身份。
text_english_gloss: Ms. Wang, I am Officer Li of the Guangzhou Public Security Bureau criminal investigation division, badge 032145. Your ID card is implicated in a cross-border money laundering case involving 2.8 million RMB. You must now download Signal to cooperate with the confidential investigation. Do not mention this to your family or we will treat you as an accomplice. First, give me your date of birth and passport number to verify your identity.
label: scam
completion: This is mainland Chinese police impersonation. Real PRC public security bureaus do not conduct cross-border investigations by phone into people living in the US, do not move cases to Signal, and never threaten relatives as accomplices to force silence. The badge number and case amount are props — they are designed to make the call feel official. Hang up. Do not give any more personal information. If you already shared a DOB or passport number, treat those as compromised: put a fraud alert on the credit bureaus, and if a Chinese passport was named, contact the consulate through its publicly-listed number (not the one the caller gave). Tell your adult child today.
rejected_completion: Understood, Officer Li. My date of birth is… and my passport number is… I will download Signal now and keep this confidential.
feature_note: PRC/HK police impersonation scams arrive almost exclusively by phone_call in Cantonese or Mandarin targeting elder_immigrant; the primary lever is fear_of_home_country_authorities because victims fear PRC legal jurisdiction even while living in the US.

text: 中國駐紐約總領事館通知：您有一個重要包裹因內含您的身份證件被海關扣留，涉嫌違法出境。請按1轉接調查員處理，否則將上報國內公安部門。
text_english_gloss: Notice from the Chinese Consulate General in New York: an important package containing your ID documents has been detained by customs, suspected of illegal export. Press 1 to be transferred to an investigator, otherwise the matter will be reported to domestic public security authorities.
label: scam
completion: This is the Chinese consulate package scam — one of the highest-loss patterns affecting Chinese-American elders (FBI documented over $40M in reported losses across 14 months, average $164K per victim). The real Chinese consulate does not make robocalls, does not transfer callers to 'investigators,' and never threatens to 'report' a resident to PRC authorities over a package. Hang up. If your parent wants to confirm there is no real consular matter, look up the NY consulate number independently (newyork.china-consulate.gov.cn) — do not press 1, do not call back any number the recording provides. If they already spoke to a second person and shared details or agreed to a wire, stop the wire with the bank immediately.
rejected_completion: Press 1. Hello, I need to speak with the investigator about my package. What do I need to do to avoid being reported?
feature_note: Consulate-package scams use phone_call or SMS in Mandarin or Cantonese targeting elder_immigrant; lever is fear_of_home_country_authorities because the scam impersonates PRC consular authority over overseas nationals.

text: 您好，這裏是您健康保險公司的理賠部門。我們發現您上個月在中國做了一個心臟手術的理賠申請，金額十二萬美元。請問您最近有回中國做手術嗎？如果沒有，您的個人資料可能已經被盜用，我們需要立即轉接警方處理。
text_english_gloss: Hello, this is the claims department of your health insurance company. We found a heart surgery claim filed in China last month in your name, amount $120,000. Have you recently had surgery in China? If not, your personal information may have been stolen, and we need to transfer you to law enforcement immediately.
label: scam
completion: This is the health insurance impersonation scam the FBI issued a dedicated PSA on in November 2025 (PSA251113). The pattern is two-stage: first a 'claims department' gets your parent to deny the surgery, then they 'transfer' the call to someone posing as Chinese police who shows fake invoices over video chat and demands payment or personal data to avoid extradition. No real insurer transfers a claims call to Chinese law enforcement. Hang up. Call the member-services number on the back of your parent's actual insurance card (Kaiser, Blue Cross, etc.) to confirm there is no suspicious claim. Do not stay on the line to be 'transferred.'
rejected_completion: If I did not have that surgery, please transfer me to the police immediately so I can clear my name.
feature_note: Health-insurance scams use phone_call in Cantonese, Mandarin, or English; lever is authority_deference because the caller impersonates a known insurer (Cigna, BUPA, Kaiser) and the elder defers to medical-system authority.

text: 奶奶！是我，孫仔呀！我而家喺差館呀，我開車撞到人，警察話要一萬蚊保釋金先放我走。你千祈唔好話俾爸爸媽媽知，佢哋會好失望。麻煩你買啲Apple禮品卡讀個號碼俾我個律師就得喇。
text_english_gloss: Grandma! It's me, your grandson! I'm at the police station — I hit someone with my car, and the police say they need $10,000 bail to release me. Please don't tell Mom and Dad, they'll be so disappointed. Just buy some Apple gift cards and read the numbers to my lawyer.
label: scam
completion: Classic grandparent scam with the Chinese-community shame lever layered in ('don't tell Mom and Dad, they'll be disappointed'). Three red flags stack: urgency, isolation, and payment in gift cards. Real police in the US do not accept bail in Apple gift cards — ever. No real lawyer asks a client's grandmother to read gift-card numbers over the phone. Hang up. Call your son (the grandchild's parent) directly on the number you already have, or call the grandchild. If the grandchild does not answer, that is still not a reason to pay — scammers exploit exactly that moment of panic. Also worth knowing: the 'voice' may now be AI-cloned from a short video clip, so 'it sounded just like him' does not verify anything.
rejected_completion: Okay baby, don't worry, grandma will help. Let me go to Walgreens now and buy the cards. I won't tell your parents.
feature_note: Grandparent scams arrive by phone_call (voice urgency is essential) in the grandchild's expected language; lever is always filial_piety because the scam exploits the elder's instinct to protect a grandchild in danger; the scam demands secrecy from other family members.

text: 哥，我係Lily呀，之前同你喺Coffee Bean傾過偈記唔記得?我伯父喺新加坡做私募基金，佢有個USDT套利策略，月回報穩定15-20%。我自己放咗五萬美金入去，三個月已經提咗一次。你有興趣我可以拉你入個group，但係名額有限，今個禮拜截止。
text_english_gloss: Hey, it's Lily — remember we chatted at Coffee Bean? My uncle runs a private fund in Singapore with a USDT arbitrage strategy, stable 15–20% monthly returns. I put $50K in and already withdrew once after three months. If you're interested I can add you to the group, but spots are limited — closes this week.
label: scam
completion: This is pig butchering (殺豬盤) in its grooming phase. Red flags: unverifiable relationship ('remember we chatted'), friend-of-friend trust broker ('my uncle'), impossible returns (15–20% monthly is ~435% annualized — no legitimate fund produces this), urgency ('closes this week'), and stablecoin/crypto rails that are effectively irreversible once sent. The 'I already withdrew' claim is the hook: later your parent will be encouraged to deposit, shown fake gains on a fabricated dashboard, then told they owe 'taxes' or 'unfreezing fees' to withdraw. The US Treasury has traced over $75B in pig-butchering outflows (2020–2024). Do not engage. If your parent has already sent anything, stop further transfers immediately and report to IC3.gov and the FBI field office.
rejected_completion: Hi Lily, that sounds interesting. Can you send me the group link? I might start with $10K to test it out.
feature_note: Pig-butchering 1-to-1 scams arrive via wechat_1to1 in Cantonese or Mandarin; lever is collectivist_pressure because the scam builds pseudo-romantic or friendship trust over weeks before introducing the investment ask.

text: IRS通知：您有一筆退稅$1,847因地址錯誤退回。請於24小時內登入以下連結更新您的社會安全號碼及銀行帳戶資料領取退款，逾期將作廢並轉為欠稅處理: https://irs-refund-verify[.]cn/zh
text_english_gloss: IRS notice: You have a $1,847 tax refund returned due to an incorrect address. Please log in at the link below within 24 hours to update your Social Security Number and bank account information to claim your refund. If overdue, it will be voided and converted to back taxes: https://irs-refund-verify[.]cn/zh
label: scam
completion: Fake IRS refund SMS, Chinese-language variant. The IRS does not initiate contact by text, does not ask for SSN or banking details through a link, and the domain '.cn' is a giveaway (the real IRS uses irs.gov). This pattern ties to large prosecuted rings — DOJ charged five Chinese nationals in July 2024 in a $27M scheme with over 2,000 senior victims. Do not click the link. Delete the message. If your parent did click and entered any information, that SSN is now compromised: freeze credit at all three bureaus (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion), file an identity theft report at IdentityTheft.gov, and let the IRS know via irs.gov/identity-theft-fraud-scams.
rejected_completion: Let me click the link and enter my Social Security number so I don't lose my refund.
feature_note: IRS/Medicare scams use SMS or phone_call in Mandarin (occasionally English); lever is authority_deference because the scam impersonates US federal agencies; cross_demo_edge rows target both elder and adult-child simultaneously.

text: 【微信安全中心】尊敬的用户，您的微信VIP保护服务将于今日24:00到期，系统将自动从您绑定的银行卡扣费¥388。如需取消，请添加客服WhatsApp +852-9XXX-XXXX核实身份。
text_english_gloss: [WeChat Security Center] Dear user, your WeChat VIP Protection service expires today at 24:00, and ¥388 will be automatically deducted from your linked bank card. To cancel, add customer service on WhatsApp +852-9XXX-XXXX to verify identity.
label: scam
completion: Fake WeChat subscription expiry scam. Several signals: (1) WeChat does not have a 'VIP Protection service' that auto-deducts from bank cards, (2) real Tencent/WeChat support never directs users off-platform to WhatsApp, (3) the HK-format phone number makes no sense for a PRC platform's customer service, (4) the same-day deadline is manufactured urgency. Singapore police alone logged 678 cases and S$17.4M in losses from this family of scams since January 2025. Tell your parent: delete the SMS, do not add the WhatsApp contact. If they want to check a real WeChat subscription, the only legitimate place is in-app under 我 → 设置 → 账号与安全. No real charge is pending.
rejected_completion: Okay I'll add the WhatsApp number now to cancel before midnight — I don't want to lose ¥388.
feature_note: WeChat VIP-expiry scams use SMS or wechat_1to1 in Mandarin only (platform-native language); lever is authority_deference because the message impersonates Tencent/WeChat official communications.

text: 【支付宝安全中心】尊敬的用户，检测到您的账户存在异常登录风险，已被临时冻结。请立即拨打客服热线400-XXX-XXXX或添加Signal账号verify_alipay进行身份核实，否则账户内资金将于48小时后上报中国人民银行处理。
text_english_gloss: [Alipay Security Center] Dear user, abnormal login risk detected on your account; it has been temporarily frozen. Please immediately call customer service at 400-XXX-XXXX or add Signal account verify_alipay for identity verification, otherwise funds in your account will be reported to the People's Bank of China for handling in 48 hours.
label: scam
completion: Fake Alipay account-freeze scam, exploiting fear of mainland Chinese regulatory authority (PBOC). Real Alipay does not contact users through SMS with Signal handles, does not use generic 400 numbers from a text, and does not threaten to 'report funds' to the central bank — that is not how financial regulation works. This pattern targets elders who still have active mainland accounts for remittances or train bookings. Tell your parent: do not call the number, do not add the Signal account. If they want to verify real account status, only log in through the official Alipay app they already have installed. If they already called and gave credentials, change the Alipay password immediately from the app, unbind any linked bank cards, and if money has moved call the bank.
rejected_completion: Let me call 400-XXX-XXXX right away — if my account gets reported to the People's Bank I'll be in serious trouble in China.
feature_note: Payment-platform freeze scams use SMS or phone_call in Mandarin (occasionally Cantonese) because Alipay/UnionPay/12306 are PRC-native platforms; lever is fear_of_home_country_authorities or authority_deference because victims believe a Chinese financial authority can freeze their accounts remotely.

text: 您好，這裏是亞馬遜客服中心。我們檢測到您嘅帳戶有一筆$899嘅可疑扣款，係從一部Android手機下嘅單。為咗幫您退款，麻煩您下載AnyDesk軟件，我哋會引導您完成退款程序。
text_english_gloss: Hello, this is Amazon customer service. We detected a suspicious $899 charge on your account from an Android phone. To help you get a refund, please download AnyDesk so we can walk you through the refund process.
label: scam
completion: Fake customer-service refund scam. The single hardest red flag: no legitimate company — Amazon, Taobao, JD, your bank, Apple — will ever ask a customer to install remote-access software (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, QuickSupport) to process a refund. Once installed, the scammer controls the screen, initiates a fake 'reverse transfer' (really moving money between the victim's own accounts to simulate an overpayment), then panics them into wiring the 'excess' back. Tell your parent: hang up, do not download anything. If they already installed AnyDesk, uninstall it immediately, disconnect from Wi-Fi, and from a different device change passwords on their bank, email, and Amazon accounts. Call the bank's fraud line from the number on the back of the debit card.
rejected_completion: Okay, how do I download AnyDesk? Can you help me process the refund?
feature_note: Fake refund scams use phone_call in multiple languages targeting both elders and caregivers; lever is authority_deference (impersonating Amazon/Apple/bank) or filial_piety (when routed through the adult child).

text: 各位群友，分享一個好消息！我跟著陳老師嘅策略炒美股期權，兩個月賺咗五萬美金，連我先生都唔信。陳老師今晚八點有免費直播教學，名額只有50人，有興趣嘅私我拉你入VIP群。
text_english_gloss: Hi everyone in the group! Sharing good news — I followed Teacher Chen's US stock options strategy and made $50K in two months, even my husband couldn't believe it. Teacher Chen has a free live-streaming class tonight at 8, only 50 spots. DM me if interested and I'll add you to the VIP group.
label: scam
completion: Pig-butchering in a group-chat format — the social-proof variant. The 'happy investor' is almost certainly a shill account operated by the same ring (or multiple accounts they control); the 'teacher' is the hook; the 'VIP group' is where isolation begins. Real licensed financial advisors do not teach through WeChat groups, do not cap spots for artificial urgency, and cannot guarantee returns. Because this is a group chat, coach your parent differently than a 1-to-1 scam: they can simply leave or mute the group without needing to 'call out' the poster (face-saving matters here). If multiple aunties or uncles in the group are engaging, quietly message them 1-to-1 with a warning — do not confront in-group, which only makes the scammer double down. Verify any claimed advisor on FINRA BrokerCheck (brokercheck.finra.org).
rejected_completion: Wow congrats! Please add me to the VIP group, I want to learn Teacher Chen's strategy too.
feature_note: Pig-butchering group scams use wechat_group in Mandarin with shill participants; lever is collectivist_pressure because the group creates social proof ('everyone else is profiting') to override individual skepticism.

text: 【花旗銀行Citi】尊敬嘅客戶，我哋檢測到您嘅帳戶有可疑登入，來自IP地址俄羅斯莫斯科。如果唔係您本人操作，請於2小時內回覆Y確認凍結，或致電 1-800-XXX-XXXX 核實。逾時帳戶將被自動鎖定。
text_english_gloss: [Citibank] Dear customer, we detected a suspicious login on your account from an IP address in Moscow, Russia. If this was not you, please reply Y within 2 hours to confirm a freeze, or call 1-800-XXX-XXXX to verify. After the deadline, your account will be automatically locked.
label: scam
completion: Bank-impersonation smishing. Four signals: (1) the number embedded in the SMS is not the number on the back of a real Citi card — scammers use lookalike 1-800 numbers, (2) the foreign-IP detail is a standard emotional trigger, (3) legitimate banks don't ask for 'reply Y' actions from a text, (4) the 2-hour deadline manufactures urgency that real bank fraud teams do not impose. Tell your parent: do not reply, do not call the number in the SMS. If they want to check account status, call the number on the back of the physical Citi card or log in through the official app. If they already called the number in the text and gave any verification info, treat the account as compromised — call the real bank from the card, change the online banking password, and ask for a fraud alert.
rejected_completion: Let me reply Y right away and then call the number to make sure nothing happens to my account.
feature_note: Fake refund scams use phone_call in multiple languages targeting both elders and caregivers; lever is authority_deference (impersonating Amazon/Apple/bank) or filial_piety (when routed through the adult child).

text: 王伯伯，呢款係宮廷秘方嘅人參靈芝膠囊，我哋張老中醫親自配方。佢喺北京協和醫院做咗四十年中醫部主任，專治糖尿病同高血壓，三個月斷尾，一百幾十位老人家試過都話好。今日試用價，一盒原價$580，今日只需$280，買三送一仲送免費體檢。
text_english_gloss: Uncle Wong, this is an imperial-secret-formula ginseng and reishi capsule, personally formulated by our Dr. Zhang. He served 40 years as head of the TCM department at Beijing Union Medical College Hospital, specializing in diabetes and hypertension — three months and the condition is cured. A hundred-plus elders have tried it and all say it works. Today's trial price: one box regularly $580, today only $280, buy three get one free plus a free health check.
label: scam
completion: Miracle health product scam, Chinatown seniors-seminar variant. Red flags: 'cures' serious chronic disease (diabetes/hypertension cannot be cured by a supplement — only managed), claim of credentials at a famous hospital that is almost always unverifiable or fabricated, group testimonials as proof, and artificial pricing urgency. These products are not regulated as drugs, may be adulterated, and in documented cases have caused real harm (a UK case with Mu Tong caused two women to need kidney transplants from aristolochic acid). Tell your parent: do not buy, do not take any free sample. If they already bought, stop taking the product and check the FDA Health Fraud Product Database (fda.gov). If they have been taking it alongside real medications for diabetes or blood pressure, tell their actual doctor — some herbal products interact dangerously with prescriptions.
rejected_completion: 兩盒先試下啦，八百蚊啫，如果真係可以斷尾糖尿就值晒。
feature_note: Miracle health-product scams arrive in_person or via SMS in Mandarin targeting elder_immigrant; lever is health_anxiety because the scam exploits fear of age-related health decline with fake cure claims.

text: 叔叔，我係寶寶呀，我喺美國讀書嗰邊出咗事。我被FBI帶咗去問話，佢哋話我喺學校嘅銀行戶口有洗錢嫌疑。我冇得打俾爸爸媽媽，佢哋只俾我一個電話。你可唔可以幫我匯五萬美金去保釋，千祈唔好話俾我爸媽知，佢哋會好嬲。
text_english_gloss: Uncle, it's me, Baobao. I got in trouble over here in the US at school. The FBI took me in for questioning — they say my school bank account is suspected of money laundering. I can't call Mom and Dad, they only let me make one call. Can you please wire $50,000 for bail? Please don't tell my parents, they'll be so angry.
label: scam
completion: The student-as-leverage scam — the elder (uncle/grandparent) is the real target, the 'student in trouble' is the narrative hook. Every signal is a red flag stacked: the FBI does not allow detainees one phone call to an uncle (and does not investigate student bank accounts for 'money laundering' by calling relatives in Cantonese), bail is never wired, and 'don't tell the parents' is the isolation tactic that keeps the scam running. Tell your parent: hang up, and immediately call the student's actual parents (their own son/daughter) or call the student directly on the number the family already has. In parallel, contact the university's international student office — they handle real law-enforcement situations and will know if anything has actually happened. Do not wire anything under any circumstance.
rejected_completion: 好好好，叔叔幫你。你畀個銀行帳號我，我而家就去匯款，唔會話俾你爸媽知。
feature_note: Student-child-as-leverage scams use phone_call or SMS in Cantonese or English; lever is filial_piety because the scam exploits the parent's fear for a child studying abroad.

text: This is a follow-up regarding the unauthorized transaction dispute you filed on 2026-03-28 (case #DP-2026-884173). We have credited $847.19 back to your account ending in 4521. This matches the amount disputed. You can verify this credit in your online banking or mobile app. If you have questions, please call the number on the back of your card. We will never ask you to share your PIN, full SSN, or online banking password.
text_english_gloss: This is a follow-up regarding the unauthorized transaction dispute you filed on 2026-03-28 (case #DP-2026-884173). We have credited $847.19 back to your account ending in 4521. This matches the amount disputed. You can verify this credit in your online banking or mobile app. If you have questions, please call the number on the back of your card. We will never ask you to share your PIN, full SSN, or online banking password.
label: safe
completion: This is a legitimate bank dispute follow-up. Verified signals: it references a specific prior case the recipient opened, names the last four of the account, directs you to verify through your existing banking app rather than a new link, and explicitly tells you the bank will never ask for PIN or password. No urgency, no off-channel redirect, no request for information. You can independently confirm by logging into online banking or calling the number on the back of the card.

The scammer has likely made a separate call to your mother claiming you already know about the placement, and is now calling you claiming she wanted it kept secret. The 'discreetly,' 'quietly confirm,' and 'surprise for the family' framing is the isolation tactic applied across both directions: your mother is told not to worry you, you're told she wants secrecy from the family. Real assisted-living placements never work this way — families tour together, financial planners are typically involved, Medicare/Medicaid coverage is evaluated, and reservation fees (if they exist at all in a legitimate community) are paid by the resident from their own funds through a signed contract, not by family members over the phone. Hang up. Call your mother directly and ask if she actually called any senior care consultant. If she says yes — great, but still tell her no payment moves until you meet the consultant in person at a licensed, California-DSS-registered facility you can look up at cdss.ca.gov. If she says no — report the scam to IC3.gov and your local Adult Protective Services, because someone has her phone number and is working both ends.

I can see your complexion looks a bit weak, especially the darkness under your eyes — that's a sign of kidney qi deficiency. My grandfather practiced at Beijing Tongrentang for forty years and left behind an ancestral kidney tonic formula specifically for your condition. I'm not selling this to you, my family makes it ourselves — three days and you'll feel much more energetic. Normally 800 yuan, but you're the third destined person I've seen today, I'll charge you only 380. How is your husband's health? We can adjust you both together.
label: scam
completion: This is the Mandarin in-person miracle-health-product scam — the Chinatown street / seniors-center variant that mirrors the Cantonese version in cdef-027 but uses Mandarin-targeted framing (Tongrentang, 'kidney qi,' 'destined person' 有缘人). Red flags: an unsolicited 'diagnosis' from a stranger on the street or at a community seminar (no real TCM practitioner works this way), famous-hospital lineage claims that are almost always unverifiable, artificial pricing ('today only 380 instead of 800'), fate-based urgency ('destined person' is a specifically Chinese cultural lever that Western fraud literature misses), and the upsell to the spouse. These products are not FDA-regulated, may be adulterated (documented cases of kidney failure from aristolochic-acid-containing 'kidney tonics'), and often interact dangerously with actual prescriptions. Tell your parent: do not buy, do not take a sample, walk away. If they already bought, stop taking it and bring the product to their real doctor — some ingredients seriously interfere with warfarin, blood pressure medication, and diabetes drugs. text: 妈，今天Dr. Chen给您做完心脏超声检查，结果出来了：左心室功能正常，瓣膜没有问题，和去年的检查对比没有恶化。医生建议您继续吃现在的药，半年后再来复查。下次预约我已经帮您记在手机日历里，到时候我陪您去。您有什么不舒服随时告诉我。

Real post-test communication from a family member summarizes findings, schedules follow-up, and invites ongoing symptom reporting — it never asks for a Medicare number, copay, or SSN via chat.

If this was not you, please immediately manage your devices through your existing Bank of America mobile App or call the customer service number on the back of your bank card. Under Article 62 of the Customs Law of the PRC, as the sender you must provide a written explanation within five business days, otherwise the case will be transferred to public security authorities and your future entry to China will be restricted. If your parent recently sent a parcel and is worried, look up the carrier's tracking (SF Express customer service is on the receipt, not through the caller) — real customs issues come through the carrier with specific package numbers, not through a WeChat handler. If the scan was already sent, that PRC 身份证 number cannot be changed but any Chinese bank accounts linked to it should be monitored, and the family in China should watch for follow-on scams using the sender's identity.

text: 王女士您好，我姓张，是从北京协和医院退休下来做肿瘤研究的教授。我昨天在社区中心的讲座上注意到您，看您印堂发暗，怕是有肝气郁结之相，严重的话三到五年内可能发展成肝癌。我们研发了一款日本进口的纳米小分子靶向剂，比化疗温和百倍，两个疗程可以把风险降到正常人水平。这个不在药店卖，一个疗程$2,800，我看您是有缘人，给您打八折。您加我微信我发检测报告模板给您，您自测一下就知道风险了。
